$comment: Shared cross-language fixture for the `reference` annotation's URL-scheme
gate (docs/ANNOTATION_CONTRACT.md's 'Reference tiles'). Consumed by:
- backend/core/tests/test_session_annotations_reference.py
(reference_url_error, the gate every backend write path routes through)
- packages/ui-graph-canvas/tests/ReferenceAnnotation.test.jsx
(isSafeReferenceUrl, the renderer's own independent gate)
The two are deliberately separate implementations - the backend decides what
may be STORED, the canvas decides what it may DRAW AS CLICKABLE, and the
canvas must not trust what it is handed. Separate implementations drift,
which is what this file exists to prevent: every `accept` case must be
accepted by BOTH and every `refuse` case refused by BOTH, so a change to
either side that moves a case fails on that side.
Round 1 of the review loop found drift in both directions and this fixture
found two more while being written: the backend's lenient urlsplit accepted
hosts containing a space and out-of-range ports, and the canvas's WHATWG
parser REPAIRED `http:///path` into `http://path/` - re-reading the path as
the hostname, so a tile would have opened somewhere its author never wrote.
Both sides now require an explicit scheme://authority and a port in range,
so there is no asymmetry left to document.
The bracket forms make Python's urlsplit raise ValueError. The gate refuses
on that exception; a mutation turning it into `return None` left the whole
backend green, because no case in any list made the parser raise - so an
unsafe scheme hidden behind an unparseable authority was storable with the
suite reporting green. A well-formed IPv6 host is in `accept` so the fix
cannot be 'refuse anything with a bracket'.
